executive_summary: Welspun Living’s recovery now has supporting cash and return evidence: management reports net cash, a 44-day cash conversion cycle and 12.7% ROCE. The September quarter was achieved despite Vapi flooding, but a full-year earnings recovery and a normalized cash cycle must support a valuation already reflecting much better conditions.
research_stance: Broad operating improvement with a stronger cash position; require continuity after working-capital normalization and Vapi recovery.
results_analysis: September 2026 consolidated sales were ₹2,838.00 crore, +16.3% YoY and +1.5% QoQ. PAT was ₹170.00 crore, +1033.3% YoY and +4.3% QoQ. These percentage changes use the rounded local dataset, so small differences from company-exact growth percentages are expected.

Local operating profit was ₹338.00 crore and OPM 12.00%, compared with 6.00% a year earlier and 11.00% in June 2026. PAT margin was 5.99%. OPM is the dataset’s operating-profit/sales measure, not automatically management-adjusted EBITDA or a segment EBIT margin.

Management refers to consolidated revenue/total-income-style reporting of ₹2,870 crore and EBITDA 12.9%, while local operating sales are ₹2,838 crore and operating profit ₹338 crore/approximately 11.9%. Other income ₹25 crore and differing reported conventions mean the two margin series cannot be swapped. FY26 ROCE 6.26% in the snapshot is historical; call 12.7% is a newer management-defined measure, so the apparent conflict reflects period/definition as well as change.

FY26 annual CFO was ₹1,175 crore and free cash flow ₹726 crore. These are annual figures, not September-quarter cash flow. Latest balance-sheet borrowings were ₹2,405 crore at 2026-09-30; gross borrowings must not be confused with call net debt. Snapshot ROCE 6.26% is an older-period return measure, not a freshly recomputed quarterly return.

thesis_drivers.title: Core and newer businesses all contribute
thesis_drivers.evidence: Home-textile exports grew 18.3%, domestic business 28.2% and flooring revenue 19.3% in the call. Diversification helps, but core export programs still drive the group.
thesis_drivers.source: September 2026 local financials and current company earnings-call transcript; source links below

thesis_drivers.title: Cash conversion is the biggest improvement
thesis_drivers.evidence: Management reports moving from ₹775 crore net debt in March to net cash in September. Cash conversion cycle fell from 82 to 44 days, though the CFO says 50–60 days is more sustainable, making some working-capital cash release nonrepeatable.
thesis_drivers.source: September 2026 local financials and current company earnings-call transcript; source links below

thesis_drivers.title: Flooring turnaround has operating substance
thesis_drivers.evidence: Flooring EBITDA margin 10.8% follows 10.4% Q1, helped by portfolio/right-sizing and pricing. This reduces a drag, but management guides a steady low-double-digit margin rather than an unlimited growth breakout.
thesis_drivers.source: September 2026 local financials and current company earnings-call transcript; source links below

thesis_drivers.title: Vapi recovery provides near-term throughput opportunity
thesis_drivers.evidence: Flooding disrupted dispatches and management estimated ₹100–250 crore lost/deferred topline; restoration timing and insurance remain important. US pillow operations add another growth lever with FY29 $80–100 million ambition.
thesis_drivers.source: September 2026 local financials and current company earnings-call transcript; source links below

claim_audit.claim: September 2026 local consolidated revenue ₹2,838.00 crore, operating profit ₹338.00 crore and PAT ₹170.00 crore.
claim_audit.assessment: Re-read the current parquet and compared the report inputs. This verifies the report against its stated local data source; company-adjusted and attributable measures require the separate call/filing bridge below.

claim_audit.claim: FY26 operating cash flow ₹1,175 crore and dataset free cash flow ₹726 crore.
claim_audit.assessment: Annual cash flow was checked against the current cash-flow table. This is FY ended March 2026, not September-quarter cash flow; investing-flow and capex definitions must not be silently interchanged.

The generic financial-table funding field was re-read. It is not automatically equivalent to industrial net debt or to debt excluding leases; explicit company-specific bridges are recorded where available.

claim_audit.claim: Management revenue/total-income headline is ₹2,870cr and EBITDA margin 12.9%.
claim_audit.assessment: The local table sales₹2,838cr excludes a different income perimeter and its operating-profit measure is not automatically management EBITDA. The report keeps both definitions.

claim_audit.claim: Management says the business moved into net cash from March net debt₹775cr.
claim_audit.assessment: This describes management net debt, not a claim that gross debt and leases were extinguished. Exact cash/debt/lease reconciliation is still required.

claim_audit.claim: Cash conversion cycle improved to44 days from82 in March.
claim_audit.assessment: This is a management working-capital metric; its period and calculation differ from annual ratio-table working-capital days.
The current management return metric is distinct from the lagged annual snapshot ROCE. Reaching low teens at one interim date does not certify the full-year result.

claim_audit.claim: US onshore pillow quarterly sales grew2.4x YoY.
claim_audit.assessment: Growth is specific to the pillow business and does not mean group sales doubled or that the new plants earned steady-state returns.

claim_audit.claim: Pillow operations were around breakeven; Ohio83% and Nevada52% utilization.
claim_audit.assessment: The call identifies uneven plant utilization, limiting the inference that high growth already equals attractive segment profitability.

claim_audit.claim: Management targets US pillow revenue around$80–100m and lower-teen margin over its ramp.
claim_audit.assessment: This is potential/target economics, not current annual revenue or margin.

claim_audit.claim: Vapi processing/cut-and-sew restarted while spinning/weaving remained affected.
claim_audit.assessment: Outsourcing and Anjar supported supply. The next-quarter normalization expectation is not proof the entire site had already fully restarted.

claim_audit.claim: Management cited ₹100–250cr top-line impact from the Vapi disruption.
claim_audit.assessment: This is an estimated revenue impact, not an audited lost-PAT or recoverable insurance amount.

claim_audit.claim: Some tariff refunds had been received but were not in current P&L.
claim_audit.assessment: Customer/customs reconciliation was ongoing and future recognition was only expected. Do not add receipts to recurring current EBITDA.

claim_audit.claim: A44-day cash cycle is not a guaranteed permanent baseline.
claim_audit.assessment: Management offered50–60 days as a more sustainable range; the analyst cash case allows re-expansion rather than capitalizing the full cash release indefinitely.

claim_audit.claim: Flooring EBITDA margin reached10.8%, while core home-textile exports grew18.3% YoY.
claim_audit.assessment: Both figures have business-specific scopes. The prior official call reports flooring10.4%; group margin or export growth should not be inferred from a different category.

business_economics: Home-textile earnings combine manufacturing efficiency, customer-program mix, input-price pass-through and trade exposure. Group growth therefore needs a bridge between meters/units, realizations and new categories. The US onshore pillow strategy offers proximity and lead-time advantages, but2.4x quarterly growth is not the same as mature plant economics.

The pillow disclosure is especially informative: operating breakeven coexists with Ohio83% and Nevada52% utilization. Incremental revenue can absorb fixed costs, but the lower-teen margin ambition should be tested against raw-material, freight, labor and service-level costs at each plant. A blended utilization number hides different plant ramps.
earnings_quality: The move into net cash is supported by management statements and a large working-capital release. Cash cycle fell38 days from March. The change improves liquidity, but only the recurring part of cash generation supports a higher sustained cash-flow yield. Supplier terms, shipment cutoffs and customer advances need separate review.

Use50–60 days, management’s more sustainable cash-cycle reference, as a scenario variable rather than assuming44 days persists. At a purely illustrative annual revenue base equal to Q2 local sales×4, each10 days of additional working capital would absorb about₹311cr; this is a sensitivity, not a company cash-flow forecast.
capital_allocation: Flooring, advanced textiles and US pillow investments should be evaluated on their individual contribution and incremental capital employed. Net-cash status creates optionality but does not itself make a new acquisition or new plant return-accretive.

Vapi recovery needs two checklists: restoration of physical processing/production and recovery of customer dispatches. An outsourcing workaround can preserve volume while raising costs, and a lost-revenue estimate does not establish insurance entitlement or future profit recovery.
valuation_logic: Separate the core home-textile franchise from still-ramping categories and deduct debt/leases on a consistent basis. A recovery multiple applied to group EBITDA can overstate value if low-return growth categories require repeated investment.

The bull case requires both normalized cash conversion and new-category profitability; the base case allows some working-capital reversal; the bear case includes trade/input pressure plus delayed Vapi or US plant normalization. Tariff refunds are separately tracked until recognition and customer sharing are clear.
peer_positioning: Indo Count is a closer home-textile/export comparator than a yarn manufacturer, but US utility bedding, brands, capacity footprint and customer programs differ. Trident adds different product/integration exposure. Compare recurring EBITDA, returns on invested capital and working-capital intensity rather than a common textile-sector P/E.
